title: React Hooks Revision Notes
summary: Quick revision of the rules of hooks and the core hooks: useState, useEffect, useRef, useMemo, useCallback, useReducer, useContext and custom hooks. Ends with the common mistakes and a cheat sheet.

chapters.title: Hooks Mental Model and Rules
points: A hook is a function starting with use that lets a function component keep state and side effects across renders
React matches hooks to their state by call order on every render, not by name
Rule 1: call hooks only at the top level, never inside if, loops, nested functions or after an early return
Rule 2: call hooks only from function components or other custom hooks, never from plain functions or classes
Each render is a snapshot: props and state are fixed values inside that render, and a state update schedules a new render

chapters.title: useState and useEffect
points: const [count, setCount] = useState(0): the initial value is used only on the first render; useState(() => expensive()) is a lazy initializer
Use the functional update setCount(c => c + 1) when the new value depends on the previous one; state updates are batched and the value is not changed until the next render
State is replaced, not merged: copy objects and arrays with spread ({...user, name}) instead of mutating, or React sees no change
useEffect(fn, deps) runs after paint: no array runs every render, [] runs once on mount, [a, b] runs when a or b changes
Return a cleanup function from the effect to unsubscribe, clear timers or abort fetches; it runs before the next effect and on unmount

chapters.title: useRef, useMemo and useCallback
points: useRef(init) returns a stable { current } object; changing ref.current does not trigger a re-render
Use refs for DOM nodes (ref={inputRef}, then inputRef.current.focus()) and for mutable values such as timer IDs or the previous value
useMemo(() => compute(a, b), [a, b]) caches a computed value and recomputes only when the deps change
useCallback(fn, deps) caches a function identity; it equals useMemo(() => fn, deps) and is useful with React.memo children or as an effect dependency
Memoization is a performance hint, not a guarantee; add it only after measuring a real cost or an identity problem

chapters.title: useReducer, useContext and Custom Hooks
points: const [state, dispatch] = useReducer(reducer, init) with reducer(state, action) returning new state; prefer it over useState for related fields or many transitions
The reducer must be pure and return a new object; dispatch({ type: 'add', payload }) is the only way to change state
useContext(Ctx) reads the nearest <Ctx.Provider value>; every consumer re-renders when the value changes, so memoize the value object
A custom hook is a function named useX that calls other hooks to share logic (useFetch, useLocalStorage); each call gets its own independent state
Custom hooks share logic, not state: two components calling the same hook do not share values unless the state lives in context

chapters.title: Common Hook Mistakes
points: Stale closure: an effect or callback with missing deps reads old state; fix it by listing the deps or using functional updates
Infinite loop: setting state inside useEffect with no deps array, or with an object or array literal in deps, re-renders forever
Object, array or function literals are new each render, so they break useMemo, useCallback and React.memo unless memoized
Mutating state directly (arr.push, obj.x = 1) and then calling setState with the same reference gives no re-render
Fetching in useEffect with no cleanup lets a late response overwrite newer state; use an ignore flag or AbortController

chapters.title: React Hooks Cheat Sheet
points: useState: [v, setV] = useState(init); setV(prev => next) for updates that depend on the previous value
useEffect: deps none = every render, [] = mount only, [x] = when x changes; return a cleanup function
useRef: a mutable box with no re-render, used for DOM nodes and persistent values; useMemo caches a value, useCallback caches a function
useReducer: dispatch(action) with a pure reducer; useContext: read the nearest Provider value
Rules: hooks only at the top level and only in components or custom hooks; custom hooks are named useX and each call has its own state
